jep

Class PyConfig

  • java.lang.Object
    • jep.PyConfig

  • public class PyConfig
extends java.lang.Object

    A configuration object for setting Python initialization parameters.

    These options map directly to the options documented at https://docs.python.org/3/c-api/init_config.html#pyconfig

    This class was rewritten with the introduction of PEP-587. It contains many deprecated methods that reference the Python c-api available before PEP-587 was implemented and newer replacement methods that reference the current configuration c-api described in PEP-587. Although all methods still work the newer methods should be preferred and the deprecated methods will be removed in the future.

    Since:
    3.6

    public PyConfig setSiteImport(boolean siteImport)
    Import the site module at startup? If false, disable the import of the module site and the site-dependent manipulations of sys.path that it entails. Also disable these manipulations if the site module is explicitly imported later (call site.main() if you want them to be triggered).
    Parameters:
    siteImport - whether to enable import of site module.
    Returns:
    a reference to this PyConfig
    See Also:

  • setVerbose

    public PyConfig setVerbose(int verbose)
    Verbose mode. If greater than 0, print a message each time a module is imported, showing the place (filename or built-in module) from which it is loaded. If greater than or equal to 2, print a message for each file that is checked for when searching for a module. Also provides information on module cleanup at exit.
    Parameters:
    verbose - the level of verbose
    Returns:
    a reference to this PyConfig
    See Also:
    https://docs.python.org/3/c-api/init_config.html#c.PyConfig.verbose

    @Deprecated
public PyConfig setNoSiteFlag(int noSiteFlag)
    Deprecated. Use #setSiteImport(int) instead.
    Set the Py_NoSiteFlag variable on the python interpreter. This corresponds to the python "-S" flag and will prevent the "site" module from being automatically loaded.
    Parameters:
    noSiteFlag - value to pass to Python for Py_NoSiteFlag
    Returns:
    a reference to this PyConfig
